previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, prior stents, diabetes, and diastolic heart failure was admitted for chest pain concerning for unstable angina. Initial evaluation showed no myocardial infarction, with normal troponins and ECG. He underwent cardiac catheterization, which revealed significant diffuse disease in the LAD artery. He successfully underwent percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA) of the LAD without stent placement. He remained chest pain-free post-procedure, with stable vital signs and improved renal function. His home medications, including dual antiplatelet therapy, statin, beta-blocker, and antihypertensives, were continued. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up instructions for cardiology and primary care, and guidance on medication adherence and symptom monitoring.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ man with history of pleuritic chest pain, assess for
pneumonia.  

COMPARISON:  Prior exam is dated ___ and a prior CT torso from ___.  

FINDINGS:

PA and lateral views of the chest were provided demonstrating no focal
consolidation effusion or pneumothorax.  A stent projecting over the heart on
the lateral projection corresponds with a stent residing within the circumflex
coronary artery.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette is stable.  Bony structures
are intact.  

IMPRESSION:

No acute intrathoracic process.

HISTORY:  History of intermittent chest pain radiating to the back.  Evaluate
for dissection.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial imaging was obtained through the chest following the
administration of intravenous contrast material according to the chest pain
protocol.  Coronal and sagittal reformats were completed. Oblique reformats
were completed.

DLP: 518.

COMPARISON:  CT torso from ___.

FINDINGS:

CT chest with contrast:  The thyroid gland is unremarkable.  There are no
enlarged supraclavicular, axillary, mediastinal or hilar lymph nodes.  There
is a normal 3 vessel aortic arch.  The aorta is of normal caliber without
evidence of acute aortic pathology including dissection.  The main pulmonary
artery is of normal caliber and there is no pulmonary embolus.  Coronary
stents are noted.  There is no pericardial effusion.  The heart is not
enlarged.  Scattered small ground-glass opacities in the right lower lobe
(3:117) in a subpleural peribronchovascular distribution with a single
mucus-plugged small airway and other areas of bronchiectasis in the right
lower lobe suggests acute on chronic airways infection. There is minimal
atelectasis in the right middle lobe and right base.  There is no large focal
consolidation, pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  The airways are patent the
subsegmental levels.

This study is not tailored for evaluation of subdiaphragmatic structures but
limited views are unremarkable.

Osseous structures:  There are no concerning osseous lesions.

IMPRESSION:
1. No evidence of pulmonary embolism or acute aortic pathology.

2. Scattered small ground-glass opacities in the right lower lobe with a mucus
plgged airway and bronchiectasis suggests acute on chronic airways infection.
